note: Stop reporting things that are not true, and stop staying silent about things that are. This sweep came out of real work: nine Jira tickets were handed to agents against a live Figma file, and three of them stopped dead on devup-mcp rather than on the code they were meant to change. componentTsx on a Section link failed with DEVUP_FIGMA_NODE_NOT_FOUND and details: null, because a Section is scoped to its own subtree and an instance's component master normally lives outside it - the ordinary case, not caller error, and the same collection served tsx with exact projection and full fidelity. responsiveTsx did the opposite on the same path: no error, no failures entry, status complete, quality.projection reported not-requested for an output that had in fact been requested, and nothing to implement from; strict: true did not surface it either. Both now behave the way rawSnapshot already did - a request that cannot be served says what it is, why, and what to do instead - and where a projection can degrade it degrades to a partial result carrying the ids that failed rather than throwing the whole export away. An asset that failed with DEVUP_ASSET_NODE_HIDDEN sat inside a response whose top level said status complete, isError false, failures empty; per-asset and per-frame failures are now aggregated upward, and a partial export says so. devup_figma_search accepted a node-id and searched the whole file anyway, returning same-named nodes from other pages - a caller building frameIds from that result implements the wrong screen - so matches are now scoped to the linked subtree, the scope actually applied is named in the response, and the search script can take a non-PAGE root instead of paying for a page-catalog walk. devup_figma_explore raised limit from 30 to 33 and returned fewer candidates, 23 down to 18, with truncated flipping to true: limit was multiplied into a projection budget that text previews then consumed, so an informational flag silently reduced results. limit is now the number of candidates returned, the preview budget is separate, and truncation reports projection and candidates apart with the reason. Reusing a cached artifactId lost the frame selection and fell back to selection_required with the whole candidate list; the selection is retained. A resource link pointed at a manifest that did not carry its own chunk uris, so the recommended delivery path for large outputs dead-ended unless the caller separately discovered the uri template; chunks are addressable from the manifest. devup_stack_diff reported 194 drifts on a project with none: identical routes were filed twice, once per spelling, because Vespera writes kebab-case paths and parameters into openapi.json while the routes are snake_case in Rust - devup-mcp was not normalizing, not over-normalizing as first supposed - and module-root routes differed only by a trailing slash. Spelling and slash are folded for the comparison key only, reported strings stay verbatim, and the count folded that way is disclosed. The same class was found and fixed in three more layers: sea-orm relation accessors were counted as missing columns, r# raw identifiers were read as part of a name, camelCase client parameters were compared against kebab-case spec paths, and a models directory holding no Vespertide models was reported as drift. devup_ui_validate warned that a hardcoded length should use a token in a project whose theme defines no length tokens at all, while missing hardcoded colours entirely because the bg shorthand was absent from the colour-like property list - noise on one side, blindness on the other. A hardcoded value is now always reported, warning with the token named when one matches and informational without advice when none does. Nested checkouts are excluded from project scans across every tool, and because find_files_named returns what it skipped and why rather than dropping it, a theme that exists only inside a nested checkout is still reported as such instead of vanishing - devup_ui_validate had been picking the stale branch's devup.json as its authority, since .worktrees sorts before apps, and saying nothing about it.
